assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made it possible to propagate nuclei on forces computed on the fly from the electronic ground state, with an extended Lagrangian that avoids repeated self-consistent minimisation. It is a simple idea that changed the field: liquids, aqueous solutions, proton transfer and condensed-phase reactivity became accessible from first principles, and its influence is visible in essentially all later ab initio simulation. This is the kind of game-changing theory I want to see rewarded, and it has been tested quantitatively against experiment for decades.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by exactly two people, so the credited pair is clean and fits well within the three-laureate limit. Priority is unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and independent implementations in many codes. Recognition is well overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Parrinello is also credited on other candidates (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials), so the committee must avoid a configuration that overlaps with those entries.
The field-wide reception of ab initio MD versus density functional theory itself, previously recognised in 1998, may make some members see it as a continuation of that prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, by bifunctional PROTACs and by molecular glues that redirect E3 ligases, is a genuinely new pharmacological principle: remove the protein instead of inhibiting it. The identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained a long-standing drug mystery and opened a route to previously undruggable proteins. It already has real consequences in clinical development.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underpins molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray, Ito, Sakamoto and Kim also made important contributions, but a fair three-person configuration exists among Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Dividing credit between the PROTAC and glue strands is the main difficulty and I am not certain of every priority detail.
assessment.maturity: Concept is about 20 years old and widely reproduced, with many compounds in clinical trials. The extent of approved therapeutic outcomes is still limited, so some will argue it is slightly early, but the chemical-biology principle is well established.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit is not yet fully demonstrated by approved drugs, to my knowledge.
Credit may be contested between PROTAC and molecular glue lines, and whether Ciulli or Gray should displace one of the three.
The proposed trio mixes two different mechanistic lines, which may feel like a compound prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs to incorporate noncanonical amino acids site-specifically in living cells is a conceptually clear and enormously enabling tool. It gives chemical control over protein structure, photocrosslinking, labelling and therapeutic protein design. It is a game-changer for protein chemistry and biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems; Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes and multicellular organisms and to reassigned codons and ribosome engineering. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed, but a three-person set is defensible. Exact priority between Schultz group members and others is something I cannot verify independently.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of broad independent uptake and many applications in industry and structural biology. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether Wang should be included beside Schultz and Chin, or Yokoyama or Mehl.
Part of the work was conducted in the Schultz laboratory, which complicates individual credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling turned a difficult bond construction into a general, reliable reaction for arylamines. It is routinely used in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, so the consequences are plain. It also fits my preference for chemistry that makes complex molecules by a straightforward route.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general ligand-controlled catalytic amination in the mid-1990s and then led the ligand design that made it broadly applicable. Kosugi's earlier tin amide work is a precursor. A two-person prize is clean, though the precursor issue should be acknowledged.
assessment.maturity: Mature, in use for roughly 30 years and widely confirmed. The 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members consider it a continuation of that field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize and how novel C-N coupling is judged relative to it.
Priority of Kosugi and the extent of his credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks or donor templates, by pairing a deaminase with a programmable Cas protein. It was a chemically inspired design that enabled precise correction of point mutations and is entering clinical use. It is original and has had large consequences.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the conceptual and engineering effort; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead scientists on the cytosine and adenine editors respectively, and Nishida and Kondo reported a related cytidine deaminase approach. Liu alone would be the simplest, though a three-person prize with Komor and Gaudelli is also possible. Credit within the laboratory is hard to assign from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: About ten years old, with growing independent use and early clinical results. Reasonably mature but long-term safety and efficacy are still developing. CRISPR was already recognised in 2020, so this would be a follow-on.
uncertainties: Whether a single laureate is appropriate or Komor and Gaudelli should be included.
Relationship to the 2020 prize and to Liu's other candidate (prime editing).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and funnel theory of protein folding resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a physical picture connected quantitatively to experiments on folding kinetics and mechanisms. Fersht's phi-value analysis mapped transition states experimentally. This is theory tied to experiment, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes with Bryngelson, Onuchic and Dill developed the landscape theory, while Fersht contributed the experimental mapping. Bryngelson and Dill priorities complicate a clean three-person prize. Wolynes, Onuchic and Fersht is a plausible mix of theory and experiment, but the allocation is genuinely uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are decades old and widely accepted, though the field has since been transformed by structure prediction, which received recognition in 2024. Timeliness is somewhat diminished.
uncertainties: Credit among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht is not obvious.
The 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design may reduce appetite for another protein-folding award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Computational descriptors, such as d-band or adsorption-energy scaling relations, allow rational screening of heterogeneous catalysts from DFT calculations, and have been validated experimentally in cases such as ammonia synthesis, hydrogen evolution and methanation. It is a case of theory making quantitative predictions that are confirmed by experiment, which is the standard I hold.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the main figure for the descriptor and volcano-plot approach; Mavrikakis, Rossmeisl, Jaramillo and Scheffler contributed, and Hammer, who is not credited here, is associated with the d-band model. This makes a fair multi-person configuration awkward, and I would only propose Nørskov from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Established over about 20 years and used widely, though the predictive power for complex industrial catalysts is still debated.
uncertainties: Missing credited person for the d-band model.
Degree to which descriptor-based design has led to deployed catalysts rather than model systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a way to organise cells changed how biomolecular condensates are viewed, from P granules to nucleoli and signalling assemblies, with relevance to disease. It is a new organising principle that connects physical chemistry to cell biology, with real consequences.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne reported the liquid-like P granules, and Rosen's work on multivalent interactions gave a mechanistic framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical principles. Attribution is plausible but spread among many contributors.
assessment.maturity: Still developing. Questions remain about the physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assembly modes, and quantitative links to function are less settled than I would like. This is likely somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Debate over what counts as phase separation in vivo and which condensates are functionally relevant.
Whether the work is better placed in physiology or medicine than in chemistry.
Allocation among five or more contributors.
